newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialist sentenced over financing.
newsitem.headline: French Socialist sentenced over financing.

text.p: A French court on Thursday gave a former leader of the ruling Socialist Party, Henri Emmanuelli, a 18-month suspended sentence for illicit party financing.

The court announced the sentence hours after a Socialist-led cabinet took office after the left regained power in last Sunday's parliamentary election. The verdict, due a week ago, had been postponed to avoid interfering with the campaign.
Emmanuelli, a former cabinet minister who served as Socialist party treasurer in the 1980s and leader in 1994-95 and was re-elected to parliament on Sunday, was charged with influence-peddling.

He took political reponsibility for schemes to funnel money to the party in the late 1980s via the Urba consultancy firm, which took rake-offs on public works contracts, but said he had not profited personally and denied breaking the law.
Lawyers argued that there had been a legal vacuum at the time on political financing.

All mainstream French parties ran covert funding schemes before a 1990 law put party finances on a legal footing. Magistrates are investigating similar cases involving the centre-right RPR and UDF parties and the Communist party.
